title: Core verbs
vocabFocus: Common verbs: tener, querer, ir, hacer
practiceFocus: Create two sentences with each verb

points.title: Only the forms in today’s phrases
points.rule: You can already say who you are and what time it is. These four verbs are chunks, not a full table. Tengo is what you have, including hunger and age. Tengo que means have to. Quiero and voy are followed by a or another verb. The you-forms you will hear are tienes, quieres, and haces. Vamos and hacemos are we.

examples.english: I am hungry. I have to work.
I want coffee. What do you want to eat?
I am going to work. Where are you going?
I exercise. What are you doing today?

grammar.notYet: The rest of each conjugation, and the past tense. Leave vas, quieres, and haces as the you-forms in these phrases.

phrases.note: Tienes is the you-form of tengo.

phrases.english: What do you want to eat?

phrases.note: Por la mañana is the day 2 phrase for in the morning.

phrases.english: We are going to the park.

lines.speaker: Noa
lines.english: What do you want to do tonight?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.english: I am hungry. I want to eat.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.spanish: No tengo mucho tiempo. Tengo que trabajar mañana.
lines.english: I do not have much time. I have to work tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.spanish: Perfecto. Voy a casa a las nueve.
lines.english: Perfect. I am going home at nine.

practice.title: Two sentences each
practice.instruction: Make two sentences with tener, two with querer, two with ir, and two with hacer. Use today’s time of day in one of them.
tips: Tener is used for hunger, age, and obligation (tener que).
Keep the sentences short and spoken, not written first.
